Freedoom Phase 2 WebAssembly source and build notes
===================================================

The corresponding Chocolate Doom source snapshot is chocolate-doom-emscripten.tar.gz.
It is the browser-adapted source published in Oscar Revollo's doom-wasm repository
at commit ed01a7f3dcc9b1b42c1973d0ebfa3b482a88eb2a. The engine base is pinned in
provenance.json. Its browser changes export pause/resume, move Doom frame updates
to the Emscripten main loop, and adapt SDL's canvas/runtime exports.

Game data is the unmodified freedoom2.wad distributed in the official Freedoom
0.13.0 release. Its SHA-256 is recorded in provenance.json. The WAD contains the
Freedoom Phase 2 campaign; no commercial Doom IWAD is used. The checked runtime
stores that WAD as a deterministic gzip stream split into three static delivery
parts. The site decompresses the joined stream in memory before passing the
verified WAD bytes to the engine.

Build prerequisites: Emscripten SDK 4.0.14, CMake, Ninja, Python 3, SDL2 ports
provided by Emscripten, and the extracted source archive. Place the official
freedoom2.wad in engine/assets/freedoom2.wad. From the source repository root,
run engine/scripts/build_wasm.sh after installing the prerequisites. That script
uses Emscripten's CMake wrapper and builds the chocolate-doom target with
SDL2_mixer and SDL2_net disabled, Asyncify and memory growth enabled, and the WAD
preloaded at /iwads/freedoom2.wad. Decompress the official WAD to reconstruct
that build input; the delivered split gzip file is only a transfer optimization.

The generated JavaScript, WebAssembly, and data files are identified by hashes
in provenance.json. Denny Games has not independently reproduced those exact
binary outputs; this record does not claim a bit-for-bit reproducible build.
After compilation, the Denny Games build script verifies the original generated
JavaScript hash and applies two documented runtime patches. The
emscripten-sleep-patch.json patch holds an Asyncify sleep wakeup while the
player is paused, including during a screen wipe, and releases it on resume.
The emscripten-fullscreen-policy-patch.json patch disables Emscripten's
fullscreen-change detection because the opaque game frame is not granted the
Fullscreen API; the player controls stage sizing in its parent page. Both
patches verify their ordered input and output hashes and are published beside
these notes.
The browser bridge, opaque-frame integration, touch controls, and CSP are local
Denny Games adaptations stored in the main repository under public/vendor/freedoom
and src/games/freedoom.

Licenses and credits in this directory cover Chocolate Doom, Freedoom, SDL2,
Emscripten, and the Freedoom contributors and music credits.
